source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Based on my rough math: on a 70×50 board (3500mm²), components take about 1300mm² (~37% coverage) — that's well within normal PCB density and should route cleanly on 4 layers.

I'd prefer to keep the individual JST connectors rather than consolidate to a 2x15+10p. The modular approach is important for the enclosure, each sensor has its own clean cable, and the boards slide into rails. A single big connector with a fan-out ribbon cable would make the wiring inside the enclosure very messy and hard to service.
Since you already have all the components placed in KiCad, could you just resize the board outline to 70×50 and do a rough rearrangement? I'm not skilled in KiCad, it would take me hours to do what would take you minutes since you already have the full project open. I'd really appreciate if you could try the resize on your end.

Noted about the ESP32 on the edge, that's fine.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
some constraints I can think of:

Constraints regardless of orientation:
\- J\_BAT on a short edge (battery sits alongside PCB)
\- USB-C on a short edge (user-facing)
\- Display connectors (J\_DISP\_SPI / J\_DISP\_I2C / J\_DISP\_LED) grouped together on the edge closest to where the display flex will route
\- ESP32-S3 antenna end facing away from battery, ≥3mm keepout

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: J2, CN5, CN17, R14, R19–R21, R25, S1 sit inside the WROOM-1 "recommended antenna clear area". The critical keep-out (no copper directly under the antenna trace) is fine because the antenna overhangs the board. Just want to confirm: are you OK with slightly reduced WiFi range from those parts being in the secondary keepout, or do you want to try to clear it?

ambiguity.description: It is unresolved whether components may remain in the module's secondary recommended antenna-clear area with reduced WiFi range or must be moved to clear that area.
